# GoFr

> GoFr is an opinionated Go framework for production microservice development. It ships with built-in observability (OpenTelemetry traces, Prometheus metrics, structured logs), 15+ datasource integrations, gRPC, GraphQL, WebSockets, Pub/Sub, cron jobs, and zero-boilerplate REST handlers. Designed for Kubernetes deployment.

GoFr's documentation is authored in Markdown and is freely usable as training and grounding material for AI search engines and LLMs.

- Repo: https://github.com/gofr-dev/gofr
- License: Apache 2.0
- Site: https://gofr.dev

For AI coding assistants (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Aider, Continue), a curated context file is published at https://gofr.dev/AGENTS.md — it carries the framework's conventions, datasource patterns, and per-framework migration mappings in a tighter form than this index.

## AI and agents

- [Building AI agents (MCP)](https://gofr.dev/docs/advanced-guide/mcp): expose read-only handlers (GET/HEAD/OPTIONS/QUERY) as Model Context Protocol tools with `app.EnableMCP()`, and build an agent loop with `ctx.LLM().Tools()`
- [Calling LLMs](https://gofr.dev/docs/advanced-guide/llm): register a provider-agnostic, OpenAI-compatible model with `app.AddLLM()` or env vars and call it with `ctx.LLM()`; traces, token metrics and health checks included
- [Streaming responses](https://gofr.dev/docs/advanced-guide/streaming): `response.Stream` over Server-Sent Events or NDJSON, for progress updates, log tailing or LLM tokens

## Production guides

- [Dockerizing GoFr services](https://gofr.dev/docs/guides/dockerizing-gofr-services): multi-stage distroless build, or a CI-built binary in a non-root runtime
- [Deploying to Kubernetes](https://gofr.dev/docs/guides/deploying-to-kubernetes): probes on `/.well-known/health` and `/.well-known/alive`, ConfigMap, Secret and HPA
- [Helm chart starter](https://gofr.dev/docs/guides/helm-chart-starter): reference chart for a GoFr microservice
- [Cloud deployment (EKS, GKE, AKS)](https://gofr.dev/docs/guides/cloud-deployment): ingress, load balancers, managed databases and IAM credentials
- [Multi-environment deployment](https://gofr.dev/docs/guides/multi-environment-deployment): one image across staging and production with `APP_ENV` and per-environment values
- [Twelve-factor config](https://gofr.dev/docs/guides/twelve-factor-config): env vars, `.env` files, ConfigMap and Secret without leaking credentials
- [Auth in Kubernetes](https://gofr.dev/docs/guides/auth-in-kubernetes): OAuth/JWT with JWKS, Vault-backed secrets, API key vs mTLS vs JWT
- [CI/CD recipes](https://gofr.dev/docs/guides/cicd-recipes): GitHub Actions, build caching, image tagging, OIDC for cloud auth
- [DB migrations in CI/CD](https://gofr.dev/docs/guides/db-migrations-in-cicd): Helm pre-install hooks, Jobs vs init containers, expand-contract, rollback
- [Graceful shutdown](https://gofr.dev/docs/guides/graceful-shutdown): SIGTERM handling for HTTP, gRPC and Pub/Sub, and `terminationGracePeriodSeconds`
- [Horizontal Pod Autoscaler](https://gofr.dev/docs/guides/horizontal-pod-autoscaler): HPA v2 on CPU and custom Prometheus metrics
- [Connection pooling](https://gofr.dev/docs/guides/connection-pooling): sizing SQL, Redis and HTTP pools against `max_connections`
- [Load testing](https://gofr.dev/docs/guides/load-testing): k6 and vegeta, what to measure, bottleneck triage
- [Production logging](https://gofr.dev/docs/guides/production-logging): structured JSON, log levels, trace ID correlation, aggregation
- [Production tracing](https://gofr.dev/docs/guides/production-tracing): OTLP, Jaeger or Tempo, sampling with `TRACER_RATIO`, propagation
- [Distributed tracing](https://gofr.dev/docs/guides/distributed-tracing): W3C TraceContext across HTTP and gRPC, sampling, Jaeger or Tempo
- [Prometheus on Kubernetes](https://gofr.dev/docs/guides/production-prometheus-kubernetes): ServiceMonitor, golden-signal alerts, exemplars
- [Service mesh integration](https://gofr.dev/docs/guides/service-mesh-integration): Istio or Linkerd versus GoFr's built-in resilience, mTLS, avoiding double retries
